properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Bitcoin leg of the XMR/BTC atomic swap: secp256k1 signatures, adaptor-sig recovery keys and cross-curve scalar conversions. On-chain validation is fixed by the Bitcoin protocol (vendor-controlled); the adaptor/DLEQ scheme layered on it is first-party. Shor breaks all of it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Download-integrity pin for the monero-wallet-rpc v0.18.3.1 binary (the hash constants at lines 49-72 are a governance/pinning artifact).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Signs the swap's Bitcoin lock/cancel/refund/redeem/punish transactions. Bitcoin's chain rules fix ECDSA-secp256k1 (vendor-controlled); the swap's own use of it is first-party code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Peer identity for the libp2p swap network and the Tor hidden-service identity of the ASB. Ed25519 is Shor-vulnerable; libp2p's identity scheme (and Tor v3) are vendor-fixed. Changeable only via protocol evolution, not per-app config.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The libp2p Noise XX session carries ALL swap negotiation traffic (adaptor signatures, DLEQ proofs, encrypted signatures) — harvest-now-decrypt-later relevant. curve25519-dalek also provides Monero's ed25519-group scalar arithmetic throughout the swap.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 signature scheme shipped in this XMR/BTC atomic-swap daemon: libp2p peer identity keypairs, Tor v3 onion-service keys (torut), and swap-side signing support. Quantum-unsafe under Shor but a deadline risk (forged identities), not harvest-now-decrypt-later. First-party dependency — changeable here by bumping the crate; long-term ML-DSA-65.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 key agreement for the daemon's TLS sessions (electrum-client to the Electrum server, reqwest/rustls HTTPS, wallet RPC) and the libp2p Noise_XX transport between swap peers. Retroactively breakable — recorded swap traffic is harvest-now-decrypt-later material. ring 0.16.20 (2021) predates hybrid KEM support; migration means the rustls 0.23 line already in the lock plus a hybrid-capable backend.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Curve25519 group arithmetic underpinning the X25519 Noise handshake and Ed25519 identities in the libp2p/torut stacks. Monero's own key arithmetic in this build uses the curve25519-dalek-ng fork, which is pinned separately. Quantum-unsafe elliptic-curve group; migrates together with the key-agreement and signature layers above it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-GCM AEAD available to the libp2p Noise transport between swap peers — snow runs Aes256Gcm for its AESGCM cipher suite. Symmetric AEAD: quantum-safe in practice, Grover only halves the margin, and snow selects AES-256; CNSA 2.0-compliant as-is. Changeable here by bumping snow/aes-gcm.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC (RustCrypto, via crypto-mac 0.11) used by the Tor control/onion-service layer of the daemon (torut). Quantum-safe as a MAC — Grover gives only a square-root speedup. A second pin, hmac 0.12.1, serves bitcoin-harness and other consumers; this object is the 0.11.0 line torut needs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Integrity pinning of the monero-wallet-rpc download; the hardcoded per-platform hashes at wallet_rpc.rs:49-72 are the pinning/governance artifact. PQ-adequate (Grover gives only square-root speedup).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 digest primitive in the build — used inside the Ed25519 (ed25519-dalek), Noise (snow) and Tor (torut) stacks; the swap crate also calls sha2 directly for its own hashing (see LIB-ea6b9ac4). Hashes are the least urgent class: Grover gives square-root preimage speedup only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The AEAD actually protecting the libp2p Noise XX session (swap P2P traffic). PQ-safe symmetric cipher — no migration needed; the vulnerability of that session lies in its X25519 key agreement, not the AEAD.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Root of all long-term key material in the system: compromise of seed.pem compromises the Bitcoin wallet, the libp2p identity and the Tor onion service. The 256-bit entropy itself is quantum-adequate; every key derived from it is not.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Provides the Ed25519 expansion for the Tor v3 onion key (vendor-fixed by Tor's onion protocol). Version 1.x is the 2019-era line of the library; the algorithm, not the version, is the exposure.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The TLS provider for every outbound HTTPS session in the tree. Changeable here — the pin to rustls 0.19.0 is a Cargo.lock decision; upgrading is the PQ migration lever for all four sessions.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: First-party SHA-256 hashing by the swap crate itself — digesting protocol messages/transactions to derive swap IDs and verify wallet-RPC data. Same logical asset as ALG-928ac765 (the sha2@0.9.8 pin), referenced via same_as so a reader chases one entry, not two.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Protocol capability of the shipped rustls: TLS 1.3 with classical ECDHE (X25519/P-256/P-384 via ring). No PQ or hybrid key-exchange groups exist in this version — all TLS traffic is harvest-now-decrypt-later. Migration: rustls upgrade path to hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD for the libp2p Noise transport between swap peers — snow's default cipher for the peer-to-peer swap channel. Symmetric AEAD, quantum-safe in practice (256-bit key, Grover square-root margin only). Changeable by bumping snow.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 Diffie-Hellman for the Noise_XX handshake protecting the peer-to-peer swap protocol traffic between the two swap parties. Quantum-unsafe key agreement: recorded libp2p swap traffic is harvest-now-decrypt-later material. Migration needs a PQ libp2p transport (Noise with an ML-KEM hybrid pattern). First-party dependency, changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BoringSSL-derived crypto provider for the daemon's TLS (Electrum server connection, wallet RPC, HTTPS via reqwest/rustls): supplies X25519 key agreement, AES-GCM/ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEADs and ECDSA/RSA certificate-chain verification. ring 0.16.20 (2021) ships no post-quantum groups; PQ readiness depends on moving consumers to the rustls 0.23 line already in the lock with a hybrid-capable backend (aws-lc-rs or ring 0.17.x + KEM extensions). Kept distinct from ALG-defedad1 (X25519 via ring) because

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available AEAD option in the shipped library set (noise/rustls cipher selection). PQ-safe; inventory records availability, which the application cannot show non-use of.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RustCrypto HMAC crate in the build's Tor support — same logical asset as ALG-0db1f0bc (HMAC via hmac@0.11.0), deduplicated via same_as.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Curve25519 arithmetic crate for the libp2p Noise handshake and Ed25519 identities — same logical asset as ALG-82f1eeb2 (Curve25519 via curve25519-dalek@3.1.0), deduplicated via same_as. Monero key handling uses the separate curve25519-dalek-ng pin.
